questions.stem: Why did Spanish Florida offer freedom to some people escaping English slavery?

choices.text: Spain had ended slavery everywhere in its empire, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Spanish sanctuary was conditional and did not abolish slavery throughout the empire.

choices.text: Florida had no need for defenders or settlers, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Its exposed position made population and military service valuable.

choices.text: The offer had no connection to war with England, as an explanation of the broader historical pattern.
choices.feedback: Imperial competition gave sanctuary policy strategic force.

choices.text: Sanctuary strengthened a vulnerable border by attracting settlers, soldiers, and intelligence while weakening English rivals.
choices.feedback: The policy joined Catholic conversion, military defense, settlement, and imperial rivalry.
